title: Schwartz-Zippel (ODLSZ) Lemma, Polynomial Identity Testing, Algebraic Generalizations, and Verified Lattice Benchmarks
purpose: Primary-source research vault for the Ore-DeMillo-Lipton-Schwartz-Zippel (ODLSZ) family of multivariate polynomial root bounds, Polynomial Identity Testing (PIT), algebraic and ring-theoretic generalizations, complexity and derandomization milestones through 2026, interactive proof soundness, formal proof-assistant libraries, and exact computational bridges into SCargo's Import-Style Riemann Lattice (G_PLR) and probabilistic SWE-sweep layer.

anti_conflation_guard.attribution_rule: Credits the full four-paper founding lineage: Oystein Ore (1922, finite fields), Richard A. DeMillo & Richard J. Lipton (1978, randomized algebraic testing), Richard Zippel (1979, sparse polynomial zero-testing), and Jacob T. Schwartz (1980, sharp total-degree inductive PIT bound).
anti_conflation_guard.theorem_variant_separation: Strictly distinguishes five non-equivalent theorem families: (1) total-degree ODLSZ, (2) individual-degree DLZ/Knuth, (3) sharp finite-grid Alon-Furedi and Combinatorial Nullstellensatz, (4) Hasse-derivative Multiplicity SZ (DKSS 2013), and (5) commutative-ring Condition (D) grid bounds (BCPS 2018).
anti_conflation_guard.ring_hypothesis_guard: Classical ODLSZ requires an integral domain (no nonzero zero divisors). Over composite rings such as Z/mZ, the bound fails (e.g. x(x-1) has 4 roots in Z/6Z, exceeding d/|S|=2/6 by 2x) unless evaluation grids satisfy Condition (D): no distinct a, b in S_i have a - b a zero divisor.
anti_conflation_guard.lattice_namespace_separation: Lives in disjoint tradition PIT-SZ (IDs SZ-*) separate from RIEM-A (SRC-*), RIEM-C (HR-*), RIEM-LATTICE (RL-*), and SWE literature (METH-*). Connects to RIEM-LATTICE via explicit polynomial-identity and symbolic-matching interfaces on G_PLR.

categories.name: Founding Attribution & Core Proofs (1922-2010)
categories.focus: Original finite-field bound (Ore 1922), algebraic program testing (DeMillo-Lipton 1978), sparse interpolation & PIT (Zippel 1979, Schwartz 1980, Zippel 1993), and non-inductive univariate reduction (Moshkovitz 2010).

categories.name: Sharp Grid, Projective, Multiplicity, Ring & Slice Generalizations (1989-2025)
categories.focus: Serre-Sorensen projective hypersurface bounds, Alon-Furedi hyperplane covers, Combinatorial Nullstellensatz, finite-field Kakeya, DKSS Hasse-derivative multiplicities, BCPS Condition (D) rings, Rote's unified hierarchy, and ICALP 2025 Boolean-slice ODLSZ.

categories.name: Algorithmic Applications & Graph Matching (1967-2026)
categories.focus: Edmonds symbolic matching matrix, Freivalds matrix-product verification, Lovasz randomized matching, MVV Isolation Lemma, Agrawal-Biswas & AKS primality via PIT, and the 2026 deterministic NC bipartite matching breakthrough.

categories.name: Algebraic Complexity, Derandomization & Non-Commutative PIT (2004-2025)
categories.focus: Kabanets-Impagliazzo hardness-vs-randomness, Raz-Shpilka non-commutative PIT, Shpilka-Yehudayoff and Saxena surveys, GGOW operator scaling, Limaye-Srinivasan-Tavenas constant-depth lower bounds and PIT, Atserias-Tzameret proof complexity, and Andrews-Kush-Tell uniform PIT.

categories.name: Interactive Proofs, Sum-Check & Zero-Knowledge Soundness (1992-2022)
categories.focus: Lund-Fortnow-Karloff-Nisan Sum-Check protocol, Shamir IP = PSPACE, and Thaler's modern synthesis of PIOP and SNARK soundness grounded in Schwartz-Zippel.

categories.name: Machine-Checked Formalizations in Proof Assistants (2023-2025)
categories.focus: Isabelle/HOL Archive of Formal Proofs entries for Schwartz-Zippel and Sum-Check, Lean 4 linear PCP SNARK soundness formalization, and Lean 4 Mathlib MvPolynomial.SchwartzZippel.

primary_sources.title: Ueber hoehere Kongruenzen
primary_sources.venue: Norsk Matematisk Forenings Skrifter, Ser. I, Nr. 7 (1922), pp. 15-22
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the first multivariate total-degree zero bound over finite fields F_q: a nonzero polynomial of degree d < q in n variables has at most d * q^(n-1) roots in F_q^n (56 years before DeMillo-Lipton).

primary_sources.authors: Richard A. DeMillo and Richard J. Lipton
primary_sources.title: A Probabilistic Remark on Algebraic Program Testing
primary_sources.venue: Information Processing Letters, 7(4), pp. 193-195. doi:10.1016/0020-0190(78)90067-4
primary_sources.contribution: Introduced probabilistic polynomial identity testing for algebraic program equivalence, proving that random evaluation over a finite grid separates unequal polynomials of bounded degree with high probability.

primary_sources.title: Probabilistic algorithms for sparse polynomials
primary_sources.venue: Symbolic and Algebraic Computation (EUROSAM '79), Lecture Notes in Computer Science 72, Springer, pp. 216-226. doi:10.1007/3-540-09519-5_73
primary_sources.contribution: Independently established the multivariate zero-density bound over finite subsets of an integral domain to analyze sparse multivariate polynomial interpolation and GCD algorithms.

primary_sources.title: Fast Probabilistic Algorithms for Verification of Polynomial Identities
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the sharp inductive total-degree bound Pr[f(r) = 0] <= d / |S| over arbitrary finite subsets S of an integral domain and developed fast probabilistic verification algorithms for polynomial, determinant, and matching identities.

primary_sources.title: Effective Polynomial Computation
primary_sources.venue: The Kluwer International Series in Engineering and Computer Science, Vol. 241, Kluwer/Springer, 1993. doi:10.1007/978-1-4615-3188-3
primary_sources.contribution: Comprehensive textbook treatment of zero-equivalence testing (Ch. 12), multivariate sparse interpolation, and Hensel lifting built on the Schwartz-Zippel bound.

primary_sources.title: An Alternative Proof of The Schwartz-Zippel Lemma
primary_sources.venue: Electronic Colloquium on Computational Complexity (ECCC), Report TR10-096 (June 16, 2010)
primary_sources.contribution: Gave a non-inductive proof of the finite-field Schwartz-Zippel lemma via random affine lines reducing multivariate root counting directly to the univariate fundamental theorem of algebra.

primary_sources.title: Lettre a M. Tsfasman (du 24 Juillet 1989)
primary_sources.venue: Journees Arithmetiques de Luminy (17-21 Juillet 1989), Asterisque 198-199-200 (1991), pp. 351-353
primary_sources.contribution: Proved Tsfasman's sharp bound on F_q-rational points of projective hypersurfaces of degree d <= q + 1: |Z_proj(f)| <= d * q^(m-1) + p_(m-2), refining Ore's bound in projective space.

primary_sources.title: Covering the Cube by Affine Hyperplanes
primary_sources.venue: European Journal of Combinatorics, 14(2), pp. 79-83. doi:10.1006/eujc.1993.1011
primary_sources.contribution: Established the tight minimum-nonzero bound for degree-d polynomials on finite grids prod S_i even when d >= |S_i|, showing that covering all but one vertex of {0,1}^n requires at least n hyperplanes (and giving exact 2^(n-d) nonzeros on {0,1}^n).

primary_sources.title: On the number of rational points on codimension-1 algebraic sets in P^n(F_q)
primary_sources.contribution: Independently proved and extended Serre's sharp projective hypersurface point bound and characterized extremal configurations achieving equality, directly determining minimum distances of Projective Reed-Muller codes.

primary_sources.title: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz
primary_sources.venue: Combinatorics, Probability and Computing, 8(1-2), pp. 7-29. doi:10.1017/S0963548398003411
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the deterministic non-vanishing theorem (Theorem 1.2): if f has a nonzero monomial x_1^(t_1)...x_n^(t_n) of maximal total degree and |S_i| > t_i for all i, then f is nonzero somewhere on prod S_i; unified combinatorial zero-avoidance via ideal membership.

primary_sources.title: On the size of Kakeya sets in finite fields
primary_sources.venue: Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 22(4), pp. 1093-1097. doi:10.1090/S0894-0347-08-00607-3 (arXiv:0803.2336)
primary_sources.contribution: Resolved the finite-field Kakeya conjecture in one page using the polynomial method and Schwartz-Zippel, catalyzing the modern multiplicity method in discrete geometry and coding theory.

primary_sources.authors: Zeev Dvir, Swastik Kopparty, Shubhangi Saraf, and Madhu Sudan
primary_sources.title: Extensions to the Method of Multiplicities, with Applications to Kakeya Sets and Mergers
primary_sources.venue: SIAM Journal on Computing, 42(6), pp. 2305-2328 (FOCS 2009). doi:10.1137/100783704
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the Multiplicity Schwartz-Zippel Lemma using Hasse derivatives (valid in arbitrary characteristic): sum_{a in S^n} mult(f, a) <= d * |S|^(n-1), tightening Kakeya bounds to (q/2)^n and powering multiplicity codes.

primary_sources.authors: Anurag Bishnoi, Pete L. Clark, Aditya Potukuchi, and John R. Schmitt
primary_sources.title: On Zeros of a Polynomial in a Finite Grid
primary_sources.venue: Combinatorics, Probability and Computing, 27(3), pp. 310-333. doi:10.1017/S0963548317000566 (arXiv:1508.06020)
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the Generalized Alon-Furedi theorem incorporating both total and individual degrees over arbitrary commutative rings whose grids satisfy Condition (D) (distinct grid differences are non-zero-divisors), clarifying the exact hierarchy linking Alon-Furedi, DeMillo-Lipton, Zippel, and Schwartz.

primary_sources.title: The Generalized Combinatorial Lason-Alon-Zippel-Schwartz Nullstellensatz Lemma
primary_sources.contribution: Unified the logical implication lattice among Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (existence under maximal monomial), Lason's generalization, DeMillo-Lipton-Zippel-Schwartz quantitative lower bounds (lexicographically largest monomial), and Condition (D) commutative rings, proving no single theorem implies both.

primary_sources.authors: Prashanth Amireddy, Amik Raj Behera, Srikanth Srinivasan, and Madhu Sudan
primary_sources.title: A Near-Optimal Polynomial Distance Lemma over Boolean Slices
primary_sources.venue: 52nd International Colloquium on Automata, Languages, and Programming (ICALP 2025), LIPIcs Vol. 334, pp. 11:1-11:20. doi:10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.11 (arXiv:2507.03193; ECCC TR25-056)
primary_sources.contribution: Extended the ODLSZ lemma near-optimally from product grids to constant-Hamming-weight Boolean slices (non-product domains), proving Pr[f(x) != 0] >= (t/n)^d (1 - o_n(1)) for t = min(k, n-k) via spectral sampler and hypercontractivity analysis.

primary_sources.title: Systems of distinct representatives and linear algebra
primary_sources.venue: Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards, Section B: Mathematics and Mathematical Physics, 71B(4), pp. 241-245. doi:10.6028/JRES.071B.033
primary_sources.contribution: Formulated bipartite perfect matching (and general matrix rank of linear spaces of matrices, the Edmonds Problem) as testing whether a symbolic determinant det(B(X)) is identically zero — the canonical benchmark problem for PIT.

primary_sources.title: Fast probabilistic algorithms
primary_sources.venue: Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science 1979 (MFCS '79), Lecture Notes in Computer Science 74, Springer, pp. 57-69. doi:10.1007/3-540-09526-8_5
primary_sources.contribution: Introduced O(n^2) randomized verification of matrix multiplication AB = C via random vector projection (AB)r = Cr — a degree-1 linear instantiation of Schwartz-Zippel with error <= 1/|S| per trial (<= 1/2 over {0,1}).

primary_sources.title: On determinants, matchings, and random algorithms
primary_sources.venue: Fundamentals of Computation Theory (FCT '79), Akademie-Verlag, Berlin, pp. 565-574
primary_sources.contribution: Combined Tutte's skew-symmetric matrix and Edmonds' biadjacency matrix with random field substitution (Schwartz-Zippel) to give the first randomized polynomial-time and RNC algorithms for deciding perfect matching and linear matroid parity.

primary_sources.authors: Ketan Mulmuley, Umesh V. Vazirani, and Vijay V. Vazirani
primary_sources.title: Matching is as easy as matrix inversion
primary_sources.contribution: Introduced the Isolation Lemma to upgrade Lovasz's randomized decision test into an RNC search algorithm constructing a perfect matching via parallel matrix inversion.

primary_sources.title: Primality and identity testing via Chinese remaindering
primary_sources.contribution: Reduced primality testing for n to testing the univariate polynomial identity (1 + z)^n == 1 + z^n (mod n) via random modular polynomial quotients over Z_n, overcoming the composite-ring failure of direct Schwartz-Zippel evaluation.

primary_sources.authors: Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal, and Nitin Saxena
primary_sources.title: PRIMES is in P
primary_sources.venue: Annals of Mathematics, 160(2), pp. 781-793. doi:10.4007/annals.2004.160.781
primary_sources.contribution: Derandomized the Agrawal-Biswas polynomial identity test for (x + a)^n == x^n + a (mod x^r - 1, n), yielding the landmark unconditional deterministic polynomial-time primality test.

primary_sources.authors: Abhranil Chatterjee, Sumanta Ghosh, Rohit Gurjar, Roshan Raj, and Thomas Thierauf
primary_sources.title: Bipartite Matching is in NC
primary_sources.venue: Electronic Colloquium on Computational Complexity (ECCC), Report TR26-100 (June 14, 2026)
primary_sources.contribution: Resolved the 47-year open derandomization problem for Edmonds/Lovasz bipartite matching by placing bipartite perfect matching (decision, search, weighted), linear matroid intersection, and symbolic non-commutative rank in deterministic NC using explicit subspace designs.

primary_sources.title: On the CGGRT Criterion for Detecting Bipartite Perfect Matchings in NC
primary_sources.contribution: Simplified and sharpened the deterministic NC bipartite perfect matching detection criterion of Chatterjee-Ghosh-Gurjar-Raj-Thierauf (2026) via polynomial multiplicities and subspace designs.

primary_sources.title: Derandomizing Polynomial Identity Tests Means Proving Circuit Lower Bounds
primary_sources.venue: Computational Complexity, 13(1-2), pp. 1-46 (STOC 2003). doi:10.1007/s00037-004-0182-6
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the foundational equivalence between derandomizing Schwartz-Zippel (PIT in deterministic polynomial time) and proving superpolynomial arithmetic or Boolean circuit lower bounds (NEXP not in P/poly or Perm not in small algebraic circuits).

primary_sources.title: Deterministic polynomial identity testing in non-commutative models
primary_sources.venue: Computational Complexity, 14(1), pp. 1-19 (CCC 2004). doi:10.1007/s00037-005-0188-8
primary_sources.contribution: Gave the first deterministic polynomial-time white-box PIT algorithm for non-commutative arithmetic formulas and algebraic branching programs (ABPs), establishing a sharp separation between commutative and non-commutative PIT.

primary_sources.title: Arithmetic Circuits: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Questions
primary_sources.venue: Foundations and Trends in Theoretical Computer Science, 5(3-4), pp. 207-388. doi:10.1561/0400000039
primary_sources.contribution: Authoritative monograph surveying VP vs VNP, white-box vs black-box PIT, hitting-set generators, circuit reconstruction, and the Kabanets-Impagliazzo lower-bound connection.

primary_sources.title: Progress on Polynomial Identity Testing - II (extending Part I, Bull. EATCS 99, 2009)
primary_sources.venue: Perspectives in Computational Complexity, Birkhauser, pp. 131-146 (arXiv:1401.0976)
primary_sources.contribution: Comprehensive two-part survey (2009 & 2014) tracking algebraic geometry, depth-3/depth-4 reduction, Jacobian hitting sets, and algebraic rank methods for derandomizing Schwartz-Zippel.

primary_sources.authors: Ankit Garg, Leonid Gurvits, Rafael Oliveira, and Avi Wigderson
primary_sources.title: Operator scaling: theory and applications
primary_sources.venue: Foundations of Computational Mathematics, 20(2), pp. 223-290 (FOCS 2016; arXiv:1511.03730)
primary_sources.contribution: Solved the non-commutative Edmonds Problem (non-commutative rational identity testing / full-rank testing of linear matrix spaces over skew fields) in deterministic polynomial time via Sinkhorn-style operator scaling.

primary_sources.authors: Nutan Limaye, Srikanth Srinivasan, and Sebastien Tavenas
primary_sources.title: Superpolynomial Lower Bounds Against Low-Depth Algebraic Circuits
primary_sources.venue: 62nd IEEE Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS 2021), pp. 804-814 (JACM 2025; ECCC TR21-081). doi:10.1109/FOCS52979.2021.00083
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the first unconditional superpolynomial lower bounds against all constant-depth algebraic circuits, immediately yielding via Kabanets-Impagliazzo the first deterministic sub-exponential-time PIT for all constant-depth circuits (extended to arbitrary characteristic in CCC 2024, doi:10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.31).

primary_sources.title: Feasibly Constructive Proof of Schwartz-Zippel Lemma and the Complexity of Finding Hitting Sets
primary_sources.venue: Electronic Colloquium on Computational Complexity (ECCC), Report TR24-174 (November 13, 2024)
primary_sources.contribution: Analyzed the proof complexity of the Schwartz-Zippel lemma itself, connecting feasibly constructive proofs of root scarcity directly to the total-search complexity of constructing explicit PIT hitting sets.

primary_sources.authors: Robert Andrews, Deepanshu Kush, and Roei Tell
primary_sources.title: Polynomial-Time PIT from (Almost) Necessary Assumptions
primary_sources.venue: 57th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC 2025). doi:10.1145/3717823.3718198 (arXiv:2504.06044)
primary_sources.contribution: Tightened the Kabanets-Impagliazzo equivalence in the uniform algebraic circuit setting, proving that uniform arithmetic lower bounds are nearly both necessary and sufficient for deterministic polynomial-time PIT over characteristic zero.

primary_sources.authors: Carsten Lund, Lance Fortnow, Howard J. Karloff, and Noam Nisan
primary_sources.title: Algebraic methods for interactive proof systems
primary_sources.contribution: Introduced the Sum-Check protocol and arithmetization, proving #P is in IP with per-round soundness error bounded by deg_i(p) / |F| (union-bounded to sum_i deg_i(p) / |F| via Schwartz-Zippel).

primary_sources.title: IP = PSPACE
primary_sources.contribution: Extended the LFKN Sum-Check protocol with degree-reducing linearization operators to prove IP = PSPACE, relying directly on low-degree polynomial root scarcity for verifier soundness.

primary_sources.title: Proofs, Arguments, and Zero-Knowledge
primary_sources.venue: Foundations and Trends in Privacy and Security, 4(2-4), pp. 117-660. doi:10.1561/3300000030
primary_sources.contribution: Definitive modern reference connecting Schwartz-Zippel (Ch. 3) to Freivalds, univariate Reed-Solomon fingerprinting, Sum-Check, GKR, Polynomial IOPs (PIOPs), and zero-knowledge SNARKs.

primary_sources.authors: Sunpill Kim and Yong Kiam Tan
primary_sources.title: The Schwartz-Zippel Lemma
primary_sources.venue: Archive of Formal Proofs (Isabelle/HOL), April 27, 2023
primary_sources.contribution: Machine-checked Isabelle/HOL formalization of the multivariate Schwartz-Zippel lemma over integral domains using probability mass functions over finite subsets.

primary_sources.authors: Azucena Garvia Bosshard, Christoph Sprenger, and Jonathan Bootle
primary_sources.title: Formal Verification of the Sumcheck Protocol
primary_sources.venue: 37th IEEE Computer Security Foundations Symposium (CSF 2024) & Archive of Formal Proofs (Feb 2024; arXiv:2402.06093)
primary_sources.contribution: Formally verified completeness and n * deg(p) / |F| soundness of a modular, axiomatized Sum-Check protocol in Isabelle/HOL, instantiating the polynomial axioms over finite fields.

primary_sources.title: Formalizing Soundness Proofs of Linear PCP SNARKs
primary_sources.venue: 33rd USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 24), Philadelphia, PA, August 2024, pp. 1487-1504
primary_sources.contribution: Built a Lean 4 formal verification framework and automated algebraic decision procedure over MvPolynomial proving soundness of six Linear PCP SNARK constructions (including Groth16 and Pinocchio) grounded in Schwartz-Zippel.

primary_sources.title: Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.SchwartzZippel (Lean 4 Standard Mathematical Library)
primary_sources.venue: leanprover-community/mathlib4, Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/SchwartzZippel.lean
primary_sources.contribution: Provides machine-checked Lean 4 theorems over integral domains: MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_sup_sum (dependent product sets), MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_sum_degreeOf, and MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree (RHS p.totalDegree / #S).

theorem_families.name: Total-Degree ODLSZ Bound (Ore 1922; Schwartz 1980)
theorem_families.ring_hypothesis: Integral domain R; finite nonempty subset S subset R; nonzero f in R[x_1,...,x_n] of total degree d.
theorem_families.bound_statement: |{a in S^n : f(a) = 0}| <= d * |S|^(n-1), equivalently Pr_{r <- S^n}[f(r) = 0] <= d / |S|.
theorem_families.regime_validity: Non-vacuous iff d < |S|. Tight for univariate (x_1 - s_1)...(x_1 - s_d) with s_j in S.

theorem_families.name: Individual-Degree Grid Bound (DeMillo-Lipton 1978; Zippel 1979; Rote 2023)
theorem_families.ring_hypothesis: Integral domain R; finite product grid S_1 x ... x S_n; nonzero f with deg_{x_i}(f) <= d_i < |S_i| (or lexicographically largest monomial (d_1,...,d_n)).
theorem_families.bound_statement: |{a in prod S_i : f(a) != 0}| >= prod_{i=1}^n (|S_i| - d_i), equivalently Pr[f(r) = 0] <= 1 - prod_i (1 - d_i/|S_i|) <= sum_i d_i/|S_i|.
theorem_families.regime_validity: Incomparable to TF-01: strictly tighter than TF-01 on x_1 * x_2 (max zeros 9 vs 10 on F_5^2), strictly looser on x_1 + x_2 (max zeros 9 vs 5 on F_5^2).

theorem_families.name: Sharp Finite-Grid Alon-Furedi & Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (1993, 1999)
theorem_families.ring_hypothesis: Integral domain R (or Condition (D) ring); finite grid prod S_i; f not vanishing identically on prod S_i (equivalently deg_{x_i}(f) < |S_i| after reduction) with total degree d.
theorem_families.bound_statement: min nonzeros = min { prod y_i : 1 <= y_i <= |S_i|, sum y_i = sum |S_i| - d }. On {0,1}^n with d <= n, nonzeros >= 2^(n - d). Combinatorial Nullstellensatz gives deterministic existence (nonzeros >= 1) whenever a maximal-degree monomial has |S_i| > t_i.
theorem_families.regime_validity: Strictly dominates TF-01 whenever d >= |S| (where TF-01 gives vacuous min_nonzeros = 0). Exact deterministic regime (epsilon = 0) when evaluating over the entire grid with |S_i| > t_i.

theorem_families.name: Multiplicity Schwartz-Zippel via Hasse Derivatives (Dvir-Kopparty-Saraf-Sudan 2013)
theorem_families.ring_hypothesis: Arbitrary field F (any characteristic, including prime characteristic p <= d); finite S subset F; nonzero f of total degree d.
theorem_families.bound_statement: sum_{a in S^n} mult(f, a) <= d * |S|^(n-1), where mult(f, a) is the smallest total degree of a nonzero Hasse derivative of f at a.
theorem_families.regime_validity: Strictly strengthens TF-01 by weighting each root by its algebraic vanishing multiplicity; avoids characteristic-p division-by-factorial breakdown of ordinary partial derivatives.

theorem_families.name: Arbitrary Commutative Ring Condition (D) & Non-Product Slice Extensions (2018, 2025)
theorem_families.ring_hypothesis: Commutative ring R with identity (zero divisors permitted) and finite grid prod S_i satisfying Condition (D): for all i and all distinct a, b in S_i, a - b is not a zero divisor in R; or non-product Boolean slices {0,1}^n_k.
theorem_families.bound_statement: Under Condition (D), TF-01, TF-02, TF-03, and Alon's Nullstellensatz all hold verbatim; over Z/mZ the maximum Condition-(D) subset size is the smallest prime factor p_min(m). On Boolean slices of weight k, Pr[f != 0] >= (min(k, n-k)/n)^d (1 - o_n(1)).
theorem_families.regime_validity: Pinpoints the exact algebraic boundary where Schwartz-Zippel fails over composite moduli and quantifies the drop in safe grid capacity from m down to p_min(m).

verified_computational_benchmarks.verification_method: Exact exhaustive enumeration and arbitrary-precision rational arithmetic (zero floating-point approximation).

boolean_cube_high_degree_regime.note: Demonstrates regime where d >= |S| makes total-degree SZ vacuous (min_nonzeros = 0) while Alon-Furedi remains exact.

bivariate_condition_d_contrast.polynomial: h(x, y) = 3*x (total degree 1, nonzero in (Z/6Z)[x, y])
bivariate_condition_d_contrast.condition_d_grid: S = {0, 1} (differences +-1 are units in Z/6Z; |S| = p_min(6) = 2)

g_plr_riemann_lattice_bridge.biadjacency_matrix: B = I_12 + C^4 + C^9 (12x12 circulant, 36 edges)

edmonds_symbolic_determinant.note: Evaluating det(B(X)) at the deterministic all-1s point vanishes mod 3 and mod 5 despite G_PLR having 113 perfect matchings; random substitution over F_p avoids false negatives with probability <= 12/p.

soundness_error_envelopes.identity_name: G_PLR Bass-Ihara determinant D(u) = factored form
G_PLR full inverse Ihara zeta (1-u^2)^12 * D(u)
